messages:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] Severity: P1 - Multi-GPU collective errors (rendezvous timeouts) observed in prod serving cluster gp-pool-4. Affected service: inference-api-redwood-prod. Trigger: 5xx rate climbed + container restarts. Link: https://internal.incidents/2475019999 :rotating_light:

oncall-mike: ack. paging in SRE and runtime. I'm oncall for SRE. starting triage.

sre-ana: I'm here. seeing repeated NCCL communicator timeouts in logs on nodes gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-22. logs show repeated `NCCL ERROR TIMEOUT` then container restart.

mlops-ravi: reported from model: tp4-bert-like pipeline. Tensor parallelism across 4 GPUs. customer traffic spike around 13:42 UTC.

eng-runtime-sam: adding context: we recently pushed a kernel change in the runtime that touches NCCL timeout handling (rolled 13:15). rolling back to previous runtime would be an option.

infra-liz: checking node health now. `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep inference` shows restart counts rising on the pods pinned to those nodes. kubelet reports OOM kill on one of the containers before restart.

customer-ops-jayne: flagging customers with active sessions: two large customers ondedicated capacity seeing 502s. CX team is messaging them.

oncall-mike: quick plan: 1) isolate and cordon gpu-node-17/22 2) scale up fallback single-gpu replica set with quantized model variant 3) roll back runtime change if rollback reduces error rate. any objections?

sre-ana: agree. cordon first so new pods don't land there. run quick health checks then drain.

eng-runtime-sam: I'm preparing a rollback artifact. ETA 7m. will also increase NCCL_TIMEOUT env to 5000ms as temporary mitigation on new pods.

mlops-ravi: note: model uses KV caching and long context. increasing NCCL timeout may help but underlying OOM suggests memory blowups during collective op.

infra-liz: running commands now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 gpu-node-22
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl drain gpu-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

eng-runtime-sam: rollback started: deploying runtime v3.12.4 -> v3.12.3 to prod serving. using canary 10% then 50% ramp.

incidents-bot: Deployment event: runtime-rollback initiated by eng-runtime-sam at 2475020401. Canary 10% -> 50% in 5m windows.

oncall-mike: SRE to watch for decline in NCCL timeouts after rollback. If errors persist, we will failover traffic to single-GPU quantized replicas.

sre-ana: Observing logs post-rollback on new pods: NCCL TIMEOUTs dropping on canary pods. Older pods on drained nodes keep failing (expected).

mlops-ravi: starting traffic shift for impacted routes to fallback model shard: route 'chat.generate.large' -> 'chat.generate.large-quant-fallback' using routing rules in console. doing 25% shift now.

customer-ops-jayne: continuing customer comms: notified impacted customers, offered mitigation details and ETA. no escalations yet.

infra-liz: note: GPU memory graphs show a sharp spike before OOM on the failed pods: peaks at 98% then OOM. Could be a regression in nvtx memory accounting or an input that balloons prompt length.

eng-runtime-sam: adding a prompt-length protective cap temporarily in the router for affected models: max_tokens_per_request=2048 for the route, until we confirm. deploying now.

oncall-mike: good. getting fewer 502s overall. telemetry shows error-rate down from 12% -> 2% in the last 10m. still watching.

sre-ana: action items: - keep nodes cordoned and drained - monitor rollback canary -> if stable, proceed with full rollout - preserve failed node disks/log bundles for postmortem (do not reboot)

eng-runtime-sam: full rollback complete at 2475020900. Runtime v3.12.3 is active across prod serving.

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Error rate decreased. Paging suppressed at 2475021000 per oncall-mike.

customer-ops-jayne: customers updated: next update in 2h or when resolved.

mlops-ravi: follow-ups: reproduce locally with long context and multi-gpu setup, run stress test for KV cache growth. Add guardrails for prompt length and memory OOM in runtime.

infra-liz: will uncordon nodes only after we rebuild images and verify no remaining crash loops. preserving logs under s3://redwood-incident-logs/2475019999/

oncall-mike: closing loop for now. filing incident ticket INC-2475019999 for full postmortem and customer impact calc. assigning to eng-runtime-sam and sre-ana. thanks all. :thumbsup:
